items.title: Does `uv` support the concept of `--only main`?
items.reason: Tracks selecting only project/production dependencies, explicitly including export for dependency analysis. A maintainer recommends --no-default-groups and identifies broader production/development selection as needing design.

items.title: Option to disable all dependency groups in `uv sync`
items.reason: Reports that --no-dev leaves other configured default groups enabled and requests one flag to exclude them all. Although its example uses sync, the resulting implementation also covered export.

items.title: feat: add `--no-default-groups` flag
items.reason: Merged January 21, 2025, closing astral-sh/uv#10592 and adding --no-default-groups to export, sync, run, and tree. Maintainer comments confirm that it excludes implicit dev and configured default groups while retaining explicitly selected groups.

items.title: (Documentation) Not clear which groups `uv export` exports
items.reason: Adjacent documentation issue about export's default group selection. A maintainer confirms that export follows run and sync semantics. This concerns discoverability rather than a missing exclusion capability.

related.search_scope: Used authenticated gh to search open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs in astral-sh/uv. Separate literal searches covered export, --no-dev, dependency groups, --only-package, --no-dependency-groups, and --no-default-groups. Conceptual searches covered only main, production/runtime dependencies, and excluding development groups. Fix-oriented searches covered closed group-filtering reports and default-group PRs. PR keyword searches returned no entries, so issue timelines supplied relevant PRs for direct inspection, including comments and reviews. Inspected documentation PRs astral-sh/uv#18474, astral-sh/uv#18755, and astral-sh/uv#20520. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#10755 because its reporter confirmed a pre-commit configuration problem, and astral-sh/uv#22089 with merged fix astral-sh/uv#22090 because they concern audit ignoring --no-default-groups rather than export using --no-dev. Also inspected astral-sh/uv#11619, which concerns environment-variable controls. Checked current CLI definitions, group-selection implementation, documentation, and existing export snapshots.

type_reason: The package-only export request is already covered by astral-sh/uv#12366, and excluding all default groups was implemented through astral-sh/uv#10592 and astral-sh/uv#10618. Current source confirms that --no-dev excludes only dev and export supports --no-default-groups. No incorrect behavior or regression is established.
summary: astral-sh/uv#12366 is the canonical production-only selection discussion; astral-sh/uv#10618 implemented the existing --no-default-groups solution. The required issue-context README update was attempted but blocked by a read-only filesystem. No checkout files or GitHub data were changed.
draft_response:
`uv export --no-default-groups` covers this case: `--no-dev` excludes only the group named `dev`, while `--no-default-groups` disables all groups included by default. Groups explicitly selected with options such as `--group` or `--all-groups` are still included.

If your tracker should receive only dependencies, add `--no-emit-project` to omit the project itself.

The broader request for an explicit production-only selection is already tracked in astral-sh/uv#12366. Let's continue that discussion there.
